chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nawfali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather,
that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saddened, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) commanded him to wash his head with sidr (jujube leaves).
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do to relieve sadness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith establishes a specific prophetic remedy for spiritual melancholy, linking the physical act of washing the head with sidr to divine instruction via Jibraeel. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between ritual purity and emotional well-being, framing the use of sidr not merely as hygiene but as a sanctioned spiritual practice for alleviating sorrow.
